name: Monarch Butterfly and Pollinators Conservation Fund
summary: Competitive grants to create, restore and protect connected habitat for monarch butterflies and other at-risk native insect pollinators, plus technical assistance that gets more landowners into pollinator conservation.

geography.label: Eligible states in the monarch range

eligibility.rule: Project is in one of NFWF's eligible states
Plans to restore or enhance at least 80 acres in California or 500 acres in other eligible states
Plantings include at least one regionally appropriate milkweed species
Plantings provide at least three native nectar species in spring, summer and fall
No research funding, except data collection evaluating restoration within a larger project
Project lasts no more than two years
No grant funding for baseline legal compliance, unless enhancing existing compliance efforts

documents: Board member list, or statement that no board exists if applicable

status.quote: Monarch Butterfly and Pollinators Conservation Fund 2025 Request for Proposals - CLOSED

applicant_types.quote: Eligible applicants include nonprofit 501(c) organizations, U.S. federal government agencies, state government agencies, local governments, municipal governments, tribal governments and organizations, and educational institutions.

geography.quote: Grant funding may be awarded in the following eligible states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois

access.quote: The National Fish and Wildlife Foundation (NFWF) seeks proposals to advance pollinator conservation.

amount.quote: Grant awards will range from $200,000 to $300,000.

effort.quote: Once an application has been initiated, it may be saved and then modified and submitted at a later time, up to the application deadline of July 8, 2025 11:59 PM Eastern Standard Time.

eligibility.quote: Grant funding may be awarded in the following eligible states: Alabama, Arizona, Arkansas, California, Colorado, Georgia, Idaho, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Michigan, Minnesota, Mississippi, Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, Nevada, New Mexico, North Dakota, Ohio, Oklahoma, Oregon, South Carolina, South Dakota, Texas, Utah, Washington, Wisconsin, and Wyoming.
Proposals must include plans to restore or enhance a minimum of 80 acres in California or 500 acres in all other eligible states.
Plantings must include at least one species of regionally appropriate milkweed.
plantings must also provide at least three native blooming nectar species (in addition to milkweed) during each of the following periods: spring, summer, and fall.
Research - but data collection to evaluate restoration is eligible as part of a larger project
Funding will be awarded for projects up to two years in length following finalization of the grant agreement.

NFWF funds may not be used to support ongoing efforts to comply with legal requirements, including permit conditions, mitigation and settlement agreements. However, grant funds may be used to support projects that enhance or improve upon existing baseline compliance efforts.

after_award.quote: Grantees will be required to report progress toward project outcomes in terms of metrics selected.

documents.quote: The most important upload is your actual full proposal narrative.
